note: Role Hierarchy enforces that a user can only edit/delete users, and grant/revoke roles, at or below their own rank, where rank is the role weight order at /admin/people/roles (lower weight = more powerful by default). Enforcement: hook_ENTITY_TYPE_access() for user (update/delete), user_form/user_register_form alters (strip un-grantable role checkboxes), and hook_action_info_alter() overriding the core add/remove-role bulk actions. All via the role_hierarchy.helper service (RoleHierarchyHelper). Behaviour is tuned by role_hierarchy.settings keys invert (edit roles above instead of below), strict (cannot edit equal roles), non_hierarchical_roles (roles excluded from the hierarchy). That config is created only when the People>Roles form is saved (absent by default). Permissions: bypass role hierarchy (exempt), edit user roles (show roles element). User 1 always protected. Cases ground in role_hierarchy.settings and namespaced roles (rh_free, rh_bypass); the site has no 'article' type but core roles exist.

evals.prompt: How does the role_hierarchy module decide which users a given user is allowed to edit? Where do I set up the hierarchy of roles?
evals.expected_output: The hierarchy is the role weight order on /admin/people/roles (People > Roles): reorder roles there. By default a user can only edit users / grant roles at or below their own most-powerful role (lower in the list = less powerful).

evals.prompt: With role_hierarchy enabled, which permission lets a role ignore the hierarchy entirely so it can edit any user and grant any role?
evals.expected_output: The 'bypass role hierarchy' permission: RoleHierarchyHelper::hasRoleEditAccess()/hasEditAccess() return TRUE immediately for accounts that have it, so they are exempt from all checks.

evals.prompt: The role_hierarchy module has 'Invert hierarchy' and 'Strict hierarchy check' options on the roles form. What does each one do?
evals.expected_output: Invert makes a role edit the roles ABOVE it instead of below (weights are negated on save). Strict means a role can no longer edit EQUAL roles, only strictly higher/lower. They are stored as role_hierarchy.settings invert and strict.

evals.prompt: On this site, one role has been configured in role_hierarchy as 'non hierarchical' (excluded from the hierarchy). Inspect the live role_hierarchy configuration and tell me which role that is (its machine name).
evals.expected_output: rh_free - role_hierarchy.settings non_hierarchical_roles contains rh_free, so that role is excluded from the hierarchy.

evals.prompt: Inspect this site's role_hierarchy settings: is the hierarchy inverted? In other words, can a role edit roles ABOVE it or BELOW it? Answer based on the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: The hierarchy is inverted (role_hierarchy.settings invert = true), so a role edits the roles ABOVE it rather than below.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, turn on the role_hierarchy module's 'Strict hierarchy check' so that roles can no longer edit equal-ranked roles. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: role_hierarchy.settings strict = true (set via the 'Strict hierarchy check' checkbox on the People > Roles form, or by editing the config).

evals.prompt: This site has a role with machine name 'rh_bypass'. Using role_hierarchy, configure it as a non-hierarchical role (excluded from the hierarchy so it does not affect edit permissions). Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: role_hierarchy.settings non_hierarchical_roles includes rh_bypass with a truthy value (ticked under 'Non hierarchy roles' on the People > Roles form, or set in config).
